minutes.headline: Water district board voted to join PFAS class action and chose a consulting engineer for the Hickory Hills pilot study.
minutes.summary: The Park Commission asked about using the district's Leisure Ave land and building for a T-ball field and programming; the board was cool to it but agreed to look at a map. The board approved the May minutes, authorized the chair to sign onto PFAS class action litigation, and picked a consulting engineering firm for the pilot study. The superintendent reported a main break and a plan to connect two lines, and the board discussed whether it could help a developer extend a main.

what_happened.line: The Water District board voted by voice to authorize the chairman to sign onto the PFAS class action litigation agreement.
The board voted by voice to use a named engineering firm, as heard in the captions, as consulting engineer for the Hickory Hills PFAS pilot study.
The board will wait about two weeks for Hickory Hills input on the pilot study, and asked for a bullet-point list of expectations before a proposal is drafted.
The Park Commission asked to use district land and a building on Leisure Ave; the board said they are in use for storage, sees no sale, and will review a map.
Personnel policy changes were sent to the next meeting, and the superintendent reported seeking pricing for a directional drill to join two mains.

why_it_matters: PFAS treatment costs fall on water customers unless outside money is found, and the board said it expects possible recovery from the class action to help offset them.
Connection fees help pay the district's long-term debt, and the board found no precedent for subsidizing a developer's main extension, which bears on who pays for new growth.
